transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you too. Um, my mom actually wanted me to come see you. I hope it's okay that I'm here. She's just a little worried because... well, I guess I haven't been doing very much lately? 

I mean, I used to knit and journal, and I'd go for walks, but lately I just can't really make myself do any of that anymore. I've mostly just been staying in my room. I know I should be doing more, and I'm really trying, but I just sit there. Sometimes I don't even change my clothes for a while, which I know is probably really bad, I'm sorry. I don't mean to be lazy. It's just... when my mom comes in and asks what's wrong, I barely even have the energy to answer her. 

Is that... does that make sense for why I'm here? I really am trying to be better about it, I promise.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, let's see... I guess it's been a while now. I really hope it doesn't sound like I've just been giving up or anything, because I haven't. But, um, I think this all kind of started when I enrolled in that community college program? That was about two years and two months ago, I think. 

I was really hoping I'd do well there, but things just sort of... started slipping around then. Is it okay that it's been going on for that long? I probably should have tried harder to fix it sooner, I'm sorry.
During these past two years, have there been any stretches of a few weeks or months where you felt like your old self again, or has this low mood been present almost every single day?

Um... I really wish I could tell you yes, because I know I should be doing better by now. But... no, I don't think there have been any stretches like that. It's pretty much just been... every day, I guess? 

I mean, I try really hard to have good days, and sometimes I'll tell my mom I'm feeling okay so she doesn't worry too much, but... it's just been the same this whole time. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a lost cause or like I'm not trying, because I promise I want to feel like my old self again. Is it... is it really bad that I haven't bounced back at all?
During these past two years, have you experienced times where you had a significantly lower mood accompanied by feelings of worthlessness, trouble concentrating, or changes in your appetite or sleep?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I know I'm not doing much, which is bad, but I don't really feel... sad or worthless, exactly. I just sort of sit there. And my eating and sleeping are pretty normal, I think? I always make sure to eat when my mom makes dinner so I don't cause any trouble or make her worry more. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have those exact feelings you mentioned. I really don't want to be difficult or make your job harder. Am I explaining that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Have you noticed any changes in your personality, such as being more irritable, impulsive, or acting differently around others compared to how you were before this started?

Um, no, I don't think so... I try really hard to be nice to everyone, especially my mom, because I know she does so much for me. I wouldn't want to be irritable or snap at anyone, that would be awful. 

I guess I'm mostly just... quiet? I don't really talk as much as I used to, but I'm definitely not acting out or doing anything impulsive. I really try to just stay out of the way and not be a burden to anyone. Is that what you meant? I hope I'm not doing anything wrong without realizing it... I just try to be as easy to deal with as possible.
Have you ever had any head injuries, seizures, or been diagnosed with any medical conditions around the time this started two years ago?

Um, no... I haven't had anything like that. I've never hit my head or had a seizure, and I don't have any other medical conditions. I'm actually really healthy, physically, I mean. 

I hope that's a good thing? I know you're trying to figure all this out, and I'm sorry if I'm not giving you a clear reason for why I'm like this... I really don't want to make your job harder by not having the right answers. But I always try to be super careful so I don't get hurt, mostly so my mom doesn't have to worry about hospital bills on top of everything else. So, um, no physical stuff. Is that... does that help you at all?

Do you find that you have any unusual experiences, like hearing your name called when no one is around, or feeling like people are looking at you or talking about you in a way that feels strange or suspicious?

Um... well... I guess I wouldn't call it suspicious, exactly. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or accusing anyone of anything bad, because I know everyone at the school works really hard. But... um... since I was taking those college classes, I kind of... noticed things? 

It's just the school portal, and the people running the clinic practicum. They use these little wording changes in their emails to me, and in the comments on my assignments. It's their way of marking me as someone they don't want in healthcare. I mean, I understand if they don't think I'm a good fit, I really don't want to cause any trouble for their program. My mom says they're just regular messages and I shouldn't worry, but... I know what they mean. 

I hope it's okay that I brought that up. I really don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. I just... I pay close attention so I don't overstep where I'm not wanted. Is it bad that I notice those things? I just want to give you the right answer...

When you notice these hidden meanings in the emails and assignments, do you feel like those people are actually trying to communicate a specific, personal message to you, or does it feel more like you are just picking up on patterns that others might miss?

Um... I think... well, I hope it's okay to say it's kind of a specific message? I really don't want to sound like I think I'm super important or anything, I promise. But... it does feel like it's directed at me. 

Like, I just know that the clinic practicum people are using those exact wording changes to mark me, personally, as someone they don't want in the healthcare field. My mom keeps telling me they're just regular messages and that I'm overthinking it. And I really hate disagreeing with her, because she does so much for me and I don't want to upset her. But I can just tell what the school is doing. 

I'm not mad at them at all! I know they just want the best students, and I'd never want to get in their way or make a fuss. I just... I see what they're doing, and I know what it means for me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right... I really want to be helpful and give you the information you need.

Aside from the messages you see in the emails, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or have you ever felt like your thoughts were being broadcast or controlled by an outside force?

Um, no, I haven't really experienced anything like that. I've never heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear. And my thoughts are definitely just my own, nobody is controlling them or anything. I promise I'm not hiding anything, I just... I haven't had those things happen to me. 

I know some people with mental health struggles have those kinds of experiences, and I don't judge them at all, but I really want to assure you that my mind is my own. I hope it's okay that I don't have those symptoms to report? I don't want to make it seem like I'm not taking this seriously or that I'm not trying to be a good patient. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so you can do your job. Is it helpful that I don't have those things happening? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any times where your speech became difficult for others to follow, or where you found it hard to keep track of your own train of thought during conversations?

Um... no, I don't think I've had that happen. I mean, I try really, really hard to be clear when I talk to people, because I'd hate to be confusing or waste anyone's time. I usually just focus a lot on the conversation so I don't lose track of what we're talking about. My mom always seems to understand me just fine, anyway. 

I hope I haven't been hard to follow today? I've been trying to make sure I answer everything exactly how you need me to. I don't think I lose my train of thought... I usually know what I need to say. Am I making sense to you right now? I just want to be sure I'm doing a good job explaining things for you.

Outside of the time you spend in your room, have you found it difficult to initiate or complete tasks in other areas of your life, such as personal hygiene or interacting with friends, for the past two years?

Um... well... I hope you won't think I'm just being lazy. I really, really don't want to come across that way, because I know how important it is to keep up with things. But... it has been kind of hard lately. For a while, actually. 

I just... I mostly can't seem to make myself do much of anything anymore. I used to knit, and journal, and I'd go for walks all the time. But now I just sort of sit in my room. And... I know this sounds bad, and I'm so embarrassed to admit it, but sometimes I just stay in the same clothes for a few days. I don't mean to be gross, I promise! It's just... the energy isn't there. Even when my mom comes in and asks what's wrong, I barely have it in me to give her a real answer. I feel so guilty about it because she's so sweet to check on me. 

Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I really hope you don't think less of me. I'm trying to be a good daughter and a good patient, I just... I don't know why it's so hard to just do normal things. Does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.
When you are with other people, do you find it difficult to express your emotions, or do you feel like you have a hard time feeling any real pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I really try my best to show people how I'm feeling. I mean, I'd hate for anyone to think I was being rude or ignoring them! I always make sure to smile and let my mom know I appreciate her when she checks on me. So I don't think I have a hard time expressing my emotions... at least, I really hope I don't look blank or anything to you right now? 

And about enjoying things... I know I just said I haven't been doing my hobbies much lately, but I don't think it's because I can't feel pleasure anymore. I still think knitting is wonderful, and I still feel happy when good things happen, like if my mom makes a nice dinner. It's really just the energy part that's hard right now, not that I'm totally numb inside. I promise I still care about things! 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I still feel happy about things sometimes. I just really want to be accurate for you so I don't give you the wrong impression or mess up your notes. Am I doing okay explaining this?
